title.en: Your Mind Is the Worst Place to Store a Thought
title.de: Dein Kopf ist der schlechteste Ort, um einen Gedanken aufzubewahren

excerpt.en: The mind is brilliant at having ideas and terrible at holding them. Note-taking isn't admin — it's defense against your own memory.
excerpt.de: Der Verstand ist großartig darin, Ideen zu haben, und schrecklich darin, sie zu behalten. Notizen sind keine Verwaltung — sie sind Verteidigung gegen das eigene Gedächtnis.

body.en:
The mind is brilliant at *having* ideas and genuinely terrible at *keeping* them. It will hand you the best connection of your week in the shower and then quietly delete it before you've toweled off.

So I've stopped trusting it as storage. Note-taking, for me, isn't administrative tidiness — it's defense against my own memory.

## What the mind does badly

- Holds specifics (it overwrites them constantly).
- Retrieves on demand (it retrieves on *mood*).
- Distinguishes "I had this thought" from "I resolved this thought."

## What a note does

- Freezes the idea at the moment it was sharp.
- Externalizes it so working memory is free to *think* instead of *hold*.
- Lets me trust that nothing important is silently leaking.

## The catch

A note you never revisit is just a nicer way to forget. The system only works if capture is paired with review.

## Notes to self

- Describe my actual setup (what tool, what cadence) — keep it honest, not aspirational.
- Connect to "you don't know how you feel until you write it down" — capture vs. thinking-on-paper are two different jobs.
